question: The shared size-argument parser is a builder, and one of its builder methods narrows the parser to a whitelist of unit suffixes, so that a utility can reject the multipliers the generic parser would otherwise accept. Name every production function that configures a parser through that method, exhaustively, each as a qualified symbol of the form path::function. Exclude the file that defines that builder method, and exclude code under #[cfg(test)]; a caller in a neighbouring file of the same directory does count.

evidence.contains: pub fn with_allow_list(&mut self, allow_list: &'parser [&str]) -> &mut Self {

author_notes: An independent ripgrep enumeration of `with_allow_list(` outside the defining file yields exactly three call sites - sort.rs:354 inside parse_byte_count, truncate.rs:469 inside parse_mode_and_size, and parse_signed_num.rs:34 inside parse_count - and every one of them sits directly in a function body, so the attribution does not depend on closure or match-arm handling. The set is the only defensible answer because the question asks for all of them: dropping any name understates the fan-in, and adding one claims a call the corpus does not show. allow_list_with_all_suffixes is wrong because it only builds the list of accepted suffixes; two of the three real callers pass its output into the method, which makes it the most tempting near miss and still not a caller of the method in question. with_default_unit is wrong because it is a sibling builder method, not a caller. parse_num is wrong because head's numeric option parsing reaches the whitelist only indirectly, through the shared helper that is itself one of the three answers. ls's config conversion is wrong for the same reason: it parses a block size through a different entry point that never touches this builder method. REPAIRED 2026-09-13: the original wording asked for every function "in this corpus", which literally includes the two call sites inside the parser's own #[cfg(test)] module (parse_size.rs:951 and :965). Every arm of every run answered with those included and scored 0.667, six runs at the same value, so the question - not the model - was wrong: the gold follows the harness convention that a caller set excludes the helper's own defining module, and the question never said so. The wording now states the scope the gold uses. Archived trials answered the old wording and are not re-graded against the new one; they are excluded from any caller-bucket number that uses this question. Second restatement, 2026-09-16, after runs/cu-callers-02-confirm-20260916 missed its pre-registered criteria 3/6. The first repair named the #[cfg(test)] boundary but scoped the rest as "outside the parser's own module", and the gold counts parse_signed_num.rs::parse_count, which sits in the defining file's own directory. All three retrieval trials excluded it by quoting that phrase back and scored 0.667; all three native trials counted it and scored 1.0 - a disagreement about the question, not about the corpus. The scope is now a file boundary, and neighbouring files are said to count in so many words. validate_suite.py refuses the old wording.
